Total \(= \dfrac{20}{5}mr^2 = 4mr^2\).

129.solution:
By Kirchhoff's junction rule, at each junction the current in equals the current out.

Left junction: \(4.5 + 1.7 - 2.3 = 3.9\) A flows on to the middle junction. Middle junction: \(3.9 + 3.2 + 4.9 - 2.6 = 9.4\) A flows on to the right junction. Right junction: \(I = 9.4 - 1.9 = 7.5\) A.

133.solution:
Inductances combine like resistances. (P) series: 11 H. (Q) all parallel: 1 H. (R) \((L_1 + L_2) \parallel L_3 = 5 \parallel 6 = \dfrac{30}{11}\) H. (S) \(L_1 \parallel (L_2 + L_3) = 2 \parallel 9 = \dfrac{18}{11}\) H.

Arrangement S gives \(\dfrac{18}{11}\) H.

The power into a coil is \(P = LI\dfrac{dI}{dt}\). With the same rate of change and equal power, \(L_1I_1 = L_2I_2\).

\(\dfrac{U_1}{U_2} = \dfrac{L_1I_1^2}{L_2I_2^2} = \dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{L_2}{L_1}\).

141.solution:
The stem (cut short as printed) intends the amplitude from the second slit to be double that from the first: \(a\) and \(2a\).

\(I = a^2 + 4a^2 + 4a^2\cos\phi = a^2(1 + 8\cos^2\tfrac{\phi}{2})\), using \(\cos\phi = 2\cos^2\tfrac{\phi}{2} - 1\). The maximum is \(I_m = 9a^2\), so \(I = \dfrac{I_m}{9}\left(1 + 8\cos^2\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\).

The central maximum's half width scales from \(\theta\) to \(q\theta\), so every width in the second case is q times the first. The ratio for the first secondary maxima is \(1 : q\) (and \(q = p\)).

150.solution:
With the battery as drawn, \(D_1\) and \(D_2\) are forward biased and \(D_3\) is reverse biased (no current).

Branch \(D_1\): \(50 + 150 = 200\,\Omega\); branch \(D_2\): \(50 + 50 = 100\,\Omega\); in parallel \(\dfrac{200 \times 100}{300} = \dfrac{200}{3}\,\Omega\). With the \(100\,\Omega\) resistor the total is \(\dfrac{500}{3}\,\Omega\).

\(I = \dfrac{5}{500/3} = 0.03\) A \(= 30\) mA.
